newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity prices follow natural gas higher.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity prices follow natural gas higher.

text.p: Bulk wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) strengthened Wednesday following higher Gulf Coast natural gas prices, electricity brokers and marketers said.
Maintenance outages at several generating plants were also said to be constraining supply, helping move the ERCOT prices up, the sources said.

Startup of the Lower Colorado River Authority's 430 megawatt natural gas-fired Ferguson power plant, which was taken off line last week for a boiler tube repair, was delayed to Thursday or possibly to as late as Monday, October 21.
Also, Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 1 was out for scheduled refueling and maintenance that began in early October and was expected to last to mid-November.

Spot gas prices in Texas were said to have risen an average of 10 to 25 cents per million British thermal units Wednesday with strength from anticipated cold weather in the Midwest and a pipeline leak in Louisiana.
Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT for Thursday delivery was quoted in the $24.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range from $22.00-24.00 in Tuesday discussion, the sources said.
Off-peak ERCOT power for Thursday delivery was said to be steady at $12.00-13.00 per MWh.
November ERCOT electricity was talked higher at $20.25-20.50 from $19.75-$20.25 on Tuesday, the sources said.
December was also assessed higher at $22.00-22.50 from a range of $21.50-22.00 per MWh on Tuesday, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
